translationRepairs: In his later years caseloads swelled while clerks grew harsher and Zhao Yu deliberately eased his methods, earning a name for even-handedness.
In his later years, his caseload steadily increased.

Focus unit 至晚節，事益多 only says affairs increased in later years; clerks' severity, Yu's easing, and the name for evenness belong to the next sentence 吏務為嚴峻，而禹治加緩，名為平. The proposed cut restores that boundary without inventing content.
The dowager spoke to the emperor, who named her brother Yi Zong a gentleman cadet and posted him as interior chief of Shangdang.
The dowager then informed the emperor, who appointed Yi Xu's younger brother, Yi Zong, as a gentleman of the palace and posted him as interior chief of Shangdang.

Focus unit 上拜義姁弟縱 makes Yi Zong the younger brother of Yi Xu, not of the empress dowager. The proposal rightly improves the opening, but its after still says "her brother," which keeps the wrong kinship; name Yi Xu's brother explicitly.
The empress dowager then informed the sovereign; the sovereign appointed yixu day's younger brother Zong as gentleman of the palace, supplemented Shangdang commandery interior chief.
The empress dowager then informed the sovereign, who appointed Yi Xu's younger brother, Yi Zong, as a gentleman of the palace and posted him as interior chief of Shangdang.
義姁弟縱 names Yi Xu's younger brother Yi Zong. The proposal removes the garble but still gives only 'Zong' and leaves the appointment clause ungrammatical.
His roundup of the empress dowager's grandson Xiucheng Zhong impressed the throne, and he became military governor of Henan.
His arrest and investigation of Zhong, a maternal grandson of the empress dowager, impressed the throne, and he became military governor of Henei.
河內 is Henei. In 脩成子中, Zhong is the person's name and 外孫 identifies him as the empress dowager's maternal grandson; 'Xiucheng Zhong' is not a single personal name.
Yi Zong learned Ning Cheng had retired to Nanyang and met him at the frontier; Cheng cringed aside in welcome, but Yi Zong brushed past without nodding.

Yi Zong was transferred from Henei to serve as grand administrator of Nanyang. Hearing that Ning Cheng had retired there, when Yi Zong reached the pass Ning Cheng approached sidelong to greet him; but the new administrator, flushed with authority, showed him no courtesy.
The proposal restores the omitted transfer from Henei, but its English remains tangled. This revision preserves Ning Cheng's deferential sideways approach and Yi Zong's refusal of courtesy.
Prior sentence has 上怒曰, so bare 銜之 continues the sovereign's resentment, not Yi Zong's. Changing the subject to the emperor matches the Chinese agent.
Word reached the throne and he became governor of Hedong.
Word reached the throne and he became governor of Henei.
Focus unit 遷為河內太守 names Henei, not Hedong. The proposed place-name fix is exact; neighboring units that also confuse 河內 do not excuse leaving this sentence wrong.

The few he had not caught escaped into neighboring commanderies, and he pursued them until spring arrived. Wen Shu stamped his foot and cried to Heaven, "Ah, if only winter could be stretched one more month, I could finish my work!"

The few he had not caught escaped into neighboring commanderies, and he pursued them until spring arrived. Wenshu stamped his foot and sighed, "Ah, if only winter could be stretched one more month, I could finish my work!"
溫舒 is Wenshu, not Wenxu, and the received text reads 歎曰, 'sighed,' rather than an address to Heaven. The proposal perpetuates both errors.

After slightly more than a year—former chief of Fufeng Gongsun Yong with guest Hu Qian and others plotted rebellion—Qian falsely claimed superintendent of palace gentlemen—with several tens chariot horses—declared mission supervising robbers—stopped Chenliu relay lodge—grand administrator visited wishing to seize.

After slightly more than a year—former chief of Chengfu Gongsun Yong with guest Hu Qian and others plotted rebellion—Qian falsely claimed superintendent of palace gentlemen—with several tens chariot horses—declared mission supervising robbers—stopped Chenliu relay lodge—grand administrator visited wishing to seize.
Focus unit 故城父令公孫勇 is former magistrate of Chengfu; Fufeng misreads 城父. Swapping only that place name corrects the literal without other invention.
Sovereign because Guangming repeatedly captured great villains—summoned as grand herald—promoted Guangming's elder brother Yunnan in Yunzhong as substitute Huaiyang grand administrator.

Because Guangming had repeatedly captured major criminals, the sovereign summoned him to serve as grand herald and promoted Yunzhong, Guangming's elder brother, to replace him as grand administrator of Huaiyang.
雲中 is the brother's personal name, but the proposal leaves the literal sentence ungrammatical and obscures that Yunzhong replaced Guangming in Huaiyang.
When Emperor Xuande first rose—replaced Cai Yi as imperial clerk—because earlier as Fengyi participated settling succession policy—enfeoffed Changshui marquis.
When Emperor Xuan first rose—replaced Cai Yi as imperial clerk—because earlier as Fengyi participated settling succession policy—enfeoffed Changshui marquis.
Focus unit opens 宣帝初立; that is Emperor Xuan, not "Xuande." The proposed single-name correction matches the Chinese title.
His brother Yunnan, another bloody governor of Huaiyang, fell to petitions at the palace gate and died in the marketplace.
His elder brother Yunzhong, another bloody governor of Huaiyang, fell to petitions at the palace gate and died in the marketplace.
Focus unit 兄雲中為淮陽守 names the brother 雲中 (Yunzhong). "Yunnan" is a mistranslation of that personal name; the rest of the proposed line is unchanged and accurate.
As Excellency of Agriculture he inflated ox-cart hire from one thousand to three thousand cash per cart on thirty thousand vehicles—embezzling thirty million.
As Excellency of Agriculture he inflated ox-cart hire from one thousand to two thousand cash per cart on thirty thousand vehicles—embezzling thirty million.
Focus unit 詐增僦直車二千 raises the hire to two thousand cash per cart (from 車直千錢), totaling sixty million with half stolen. "Three thousand" contradicts 二千; the proposed numeral fix is exact.
Without Tian Yannin's advice we could never have deposed Prince He of Changyi.
Without Tian Zibin's advice we could never have deposed the Prince of Changyi.
Focus unit 非田子賓之言…廢昌邑王 names Tian Zibin and the Prince of Changyi only. "Tian Yannin" is a corrupt personal form, and "Prince He" is not in this sentence; the proposed repair matches the Chinese.
He then accused Tian of smuggling felons inside—a capital crime.
Yan Yannian was then himself impeached for admitting a criminal inside the gate—a capital offense.

After the vice-censor rebukes Yan, 於是復劾延年闌內罪人 again impeaches 延年 (Yan) for admitting a criminal inside the gate—a capital offense. Naming Yan explicitly restores the correct patient and keeps the existing person annotation reconcilable.
In this stretch 延年亡命 follows Yan's capital impeachment, and the next units return him to censorate service under Emperor Xuan. The fugitive is Yan Yannian, not Tian Yannian.
